hypotheses: iota : Type u with Countable iota is included by the section instance. s : Finset iota is fixed (empty allowed). f : iota → Real → Complex; every f_i continuous and 2*pi-periodic for the a.e. theorems. Algebraic pointwise theorem uses no continuity/periodicity premise. Each row has sum_{i in s} norm(w_i) ≤1. For the varying-row theorem W : Nat → iota → Complex and this bound holds for every natural N; no convergence of W is assumed.
scope: For the fixed countable function family, the existing countable_family_ae_convergence supplies one Lebesgue-full-measure set. On that set the finite sum of coordinate residual norms tends to zero for fixed s. For every epsilon>0 there is a cutoff threshold (depending on x,epsilon,f,s, but not on coefficient row w) after which every l1-unit-ball row has actual weighted residual norm<epsilon. Therefore arbitrary cutoff-dependent rows W(N) in that ball have residual norm tending to zero. The SAME W(N) weights both the Fourier approximation sum and the moving reference sum W(N,i)*f_i(x). Oscillating W does not imply convergence of the readout itself. Qualitative finite-family uniformity only: no rate, no growing support/family, no uniformity in x or all continuous functions.
